analysis:
This feature is not greenfield. The API already has the graphify import path in apps/api/src/rag/rag.service.ts and apps/api/src/rag/rag.controller.ts, the Project.graphifyEnabled gate, the in-memory EntityStore in apps/api/src/rag/entity-store.ts, outbox fan-out, and the Phase 1-3 event tables that Phase 4 must compose with. The work is to replace the current full delete-and-reimport path with an incremental diff backed by durable Prisma rows, add a deterministic symbol-index pipeline that consumes code_commit outbox events, and introduce a durable entity graph service so graph traversal and impact analysis stop depending on the Phase 2 in-memory store.

The main files that will change are apps/api/src/rag/rag.service.ts, apps/api/src/rag/rag.controller.ts, apps/api/src/rag/rag.module.ts, apps/api/src/rag/dto/import-graphify.dto.ts, and apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma for the incremental graph path and the new GraphNode/GraphLink/EntityNode/EntityLink/Symbol tables. The event and webhook seams are apps/api/src/outbox/outbox-fan-out-registry.ts, apps/api/src/outbox/outbox.service.ts, apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-webhook.controller.ts, apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-webhook.service.ts, apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-provider.ts, and apps/api/src/vcs/providers/github.provider.ts. Phase 4 also needs new service modules under apps/api/src/graph/, apps/api/src/codeintel/, and apps/api/src/memory/ for the new diff, AST, impact, entity, and canonical-state services.

The affected test surface is already present, which lowers discovery risk but increases regression risk. apps/api/src/rag/rag.service.spec.ts currently asserts the old full-reimport behavior and will need to be rewritten around incremental diffing. apps/api/src/outbox/outbox-fan-out-registry.spec.ts covers sequential dispatch and the existing graphify_import payload shape, so it will need new assertions for code_commit fan-out and durable entity updates. apps/api/src/projects/projects.service.spec.ts covers graphify toggle cleanup, while apps/api/test/integration/rag/entity-store.integration.spec.ts, apps/api/test/integration/rag/graphify-kb-validation.integration.spec.ts, apps/api/test/integration/vcs/vcs-webhook.integration.spec.ts, apps/api/test/integration/vcs/vcs-webhook-pull-request.integration.spec.ts, apps/api/test/integration/outbox-event-schema/outbox-event-schema.validation.integration.spec.ts, and apps/api/test/integration/events/event-write-operations.integration.spec.ts are the likely integration regression points for the new persistence and event shapes.

Key risks are consistency and isolation. Incremental graph updates must remain project-scoped and deterministic; a partial migration cannot leak nodes across projects or silently fall back to a full re-import. Prisma and LanceDB now split responsibilities, so Prisma must remain the source of truth while LanceDB stays a derived index that can be refreshed from durable rows. Parser output must be authoritative for symbol names, locations, signatures, callers, and callees; LLM-assisted enrichment cannot be required for correctness. Webhook payloads only provide changed file names, so the outbox handler must resolve file contents asynchronously before symbol indexing. Role checks and signature verification are security-sensitive, and importGraphify, indexCommit, and getChangeImpact all need controller-layer access control with webhook HMAC validation still returning 401 on bad signatures. Impact scoring must also handle zero denominators explicitly and clamp the final score to [0,100].

The migration path should be incremental: add the new Prisma tables and repositories first, then swap RagService.importGraphify() to incremental diff-and-apply while preserving Project.graphifyEnabled, then add the code_commit outbox handler and AST symbol indexing, then replace graph traversal consumers with the durable entity graph, and finally expose getChangeImpact() plus CanonicalStateService for Phase 5 consumption. The existing graphify, retrieval, and semantic-memory flows should remain functional during the transition, with Phase 2 still owning ranking and Phase 3 still owning semantic memory.

userStories.title: Incremental Graph Diff — Replace Full Re-Import
acceptanceCriteria: IncrementalGraphDiffService.diffAndApply() computes a diff and applies only the delta.
Stored graph is loaded from GraphNode + GraphLink Prisma tables, not from LanceDB.
When newNodes has 100 nodes and stored has 90, DiffResult.added equals 10 and DiffResult.removed equals 0.
When a stored node is absent from newNodes, it is deleted from both the GraphNode table and LanceDB by graphify nodeId / RAG sourceId.
When a node exists in both sets with unchanged content, it is skipped and not re-indexed.
The existing importGraphify endpoint calls diffAndApply() instead of the current deleteAllBySourceType logic.
DiffResult.indexed reflects only the number of nodes actually written to LanceDB.
A diff-and-apply of 500 unchanged nodes, 10 added nodes, and 5 removed nodes completes in under 2 seconds.
DiffResult includes durationMs for performance monitoring.
Only actors with role admin, developer, or agent can call importGraphify, and the role check happens at the controller layer.

routing.reasoning: Multiple modules and new durable persistence are involved, and the import endpoint is security-gated at the controller layer.

userStories.title: AST/Symbol Index Pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: AstIndexService.indexCommit() parses source files and stores symbol metadata in the Symbol Prisma table.
Symbol.symbolId uses the convention {repoId}:{filePath}::{SymbolName} and is globally unique within a project.
getCallers(symbolId) returns all symbols that include this symbol in their JSON callers list.
getCallees(symbolId) returns all symbols in this symbol's JSON callees list.
When indexCommit is called with files=[{path: 'src/auth.ts', content: '...'}], only src/auth.ts is parsed and existing symbols for unchanged files are preserved.
Symbol.signature captures parameter types and return type.
Indexing is triggered by a code_commit outbox event fired by the VCS webhook handler.
A commit with 20 files averaging 200 lines each is indexed in under 30 seconds.
Only actors with role admin or developer can call AstIndexService.indexCommit() directly, and the role check happens at the controller layer.
Parser failures for one file are recorded in the result and do not prevent the other files in the same commit from being indexed.
The code_commit handler resolves changed file contents before calling indexCommit(), and the webhook controller only enqueues commit metadata.

routing.reasoning: Parser-driven indexing spans new persistence, outbox fan-out, and a controller-level access control gate.

userStories.title: Ticket/Entity Graph Builder
acceptanceCriteria: EntityGraphService.rebuildGraph(projectId) rebuilds all entity nodes and links for a project.
Entity graph data is persisted in EntityNode and EntityLink tables, not only in Phase 2's in-memory EntityStore.
onTicketEvent(status_changed) updates the entity node for that ticket when it exists.
onGraphifyImport() extracts service entities from graphify nodes with type=code_module.
The initial implementation does not require a Ticket.serviceId column, and service linkage works from current Koda fields until an explicit service relation exists.
getRelatedEntities(projectId, entityId, depth=2) returns all entities reachable within 2 hops.
getIncidentImpact(projectId, incidentTicketId) returns all entities linked to the incident.
Service entities extracted from graphify inherit tags from the graphify node.
Entity graph is updated incrementally via outbox fan-out and does not require a full rebuild on every event.
A graph with 500 nodes and 2000 edges returns getRelatedEntities in under 50ms.

routing.reasoning: This is a new durable graph layer with traversal and impact analysis across multiple existing event sources.

userStories.title: VCS Webhook Handler → code_commit Outbox Event
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the existing project-scoped VCS webhook surface so push/code-intel events enqueue `code_commit` outbox records instead of doing code indexing synchronously.

**Motivation** — Push webhooks usually contain file names, not full source contents, so the outbox handler must resolve file contents before calling the AST indexer and the controller must stay thin.

**Approach** — The webhook controller stays on `POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook`, validates the provider signature with the existing `x-hub-signature-256` flow, verifies the payload has a repository identifier, `ref`, `commits[]`, and sender identifier, and enqueues one `code_commit` outbox event per commit with `{ repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }`. The `code_commit` outbox handler resolves changed file contents before calling `AstIndexService.indexCommit()`. Replaying the same `commitHash` within a 5-minute window must not create duplicate outbox rows.

**Scope** — In: webhook validation, signature verification, outbox enqueueing, deduplication, and commit file-content resolution. Out: AST parsing, symbol persistence, graph diffing, and entity traversal.

**Interface** — `VcsWebhookController` continues to own the public webhook route, and the outbox payload for code indexing is `{ repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }`.
acceptanceCriteria: VcsWebhookController extends the existing project-scoped webhook surface at POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook to handle push/code-intel events.
Webhook payload validation requires a repository identifier, ref, commits[], and a sender identifier.
For each commit in the push, a code_commit outbox event is enqueued with repoId, commitHash, ref, and changedFiles.
AstIndexService.indexCommit() is called by the code_commit outbox handler, not synchronously by the webhook controller.
If event enqueueing fails, the webhook logs the failure and returns a non-2xx response so the provider can retry.
GitHub webhook signature verification reuses the existing x-hub-signature-256 flow, and invalid signatures return 401.
The webhook secret continues to come from the project's VCS connection record and is never hard-coded.
Pushing the same commitHash twice does not create duplicate outbox events within a 5-minute window.

routing.reasoning: Webhook authentication and signature verification are security-critical, and the implementation adds an asynchronous code-ingestion path.

userStories.title: getChangeImpact API
acceptanceCriteria: GET /projects/:slug/codeintel/impact?repoId=X&commitHash=Y&changedFiles=file1,file2 returns a ChangeImpactResult.
impactedSymbols contains symbols whose file matches any entry in changedFiles.
impactedServices contains service entities linked to impacted symbols through matching Symbol.file to GraphNode.sourceFile or EntityNode.sourceId.
impactedTickets contains tickets linked to any impactedServices.
impactScore is a number from 0 to 100 computed by the formula in the design section.
When called with a ticketId, the result includes provenance source metadata pointing to that ticket.
The endpoint returns in under 5 seconds for a commit touching up to 50 files.
Only actors with role admin, developer, or agent can call this endpoint, and the role check happens at the controller layer.

routing.reasoning: The endpoint composes multiple new durable stores and is controller-gated by role checks.

userStories.title: CanonicalStateService Snapshot Read Layer
acceptanceCriteria: CanonicalStateService.getSnapshot(query) returns retrievedAt set to the server timestamp.
When ticketIds are provided, tickets contains only tickets in the requested projectId.
When timeWindow is provided, recentEvents contains only events in the window and is ordered by createdAt DESC.
activeDecisions is populated from active MemoryItem rows with kind=DECISION.
A non-existent or unauthorized projectId throws the same KodaError or Nathapp exception style used by earlier memory endpoints.
The service performs canonical Prisma reads only and does not query LanceDB, BM25, the entity graph, or other derived stores.

routing.reasoning: This is a thin Prisma read model with straightforward filtering and ordering semantics.
